question: In India, the International Day of Non-Violence is also celebrated as __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gandhi Jayanti**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gandhi Jayanti** is celebrated on 2nd October every year to mark the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, the leader of the Indian independence movement and a pioneer of the philosophy and strategy of non-violence.
 
• The **International Day of Non-Violence** was established by the United Nations General Assembly in 2007, and it coincides with Gandhi Jayanti to honor Mahatma Gandhi's contributions to the philosophy and practice of non-violence.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi's principles of non-violence have inspired many global movements for civil rights and social change.
 
• On this day, various events are organized across India and worldwide, including prayer meetings, commemorative ceremonies, and cultural programs that reflect Gandhi's teachings and values.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**, also known as the "Father of the Nation" in India, was born on 2nd October 1869 in Porbandar, Gujarat.
 
• He led India to independence through his non-violent civil disobedience movement and played a key role in India's freedom struggle against British rule.
 
• Gandhi's ideas and practices of non-violence and peaceful resistance have had a lasting impact on global peace movements and leaders such as Martin Luther King Jr. and Nelson Mandela.
 
• In India, 2nd October is a national holiday, and it is observed with various activities that promote non-violence, peace, and harmony.
